channel.title: AI Engineering — Nicholas Garcia
channel.description: AI Engineering: agent orchestration, fleet operations, and the tooling behind this site.

item.title: I Gave My Agents an Org Chart
item.description: Eleven scheduled jobs with job titles and reporting lines in a version-controlled file, a CLI for asking your manager a question, a 48-hour escalation sweep, and the status bug that told me seven of ten employees were broken when none of them were.

item.title: The Bot That Reads Its Own Transcripts
item.description: A daily loop that mines friction out of my assistant's own session logs, proposes exactly one change, gates it on a runnable check, escalates anything that can reach another human, and halts itself when the changes stop helping.

item.title: Two Memory Stores That Are Not Allowed to Overlap
item.description: One store holds rules, the other holds episodes, and the write gate on the episodic one rejects rule-shaped input and points it at the other store. Keeping them apart is most of what makes either useful.

item.title: Sixteen Automations That Run Without Me
item.description: A working inventory of the scheduled agent jobs I run: what each one does, the eight rules that let them run unsupervised, and the four incidents that produced those rules.
